source: Smart, Clowes and Clark (2025) ChatGPT, extended: large language models and the extended mind
finding: Built Digital Andy, a retrieval-augmented GPT-3.5 over Andy Clark's writings, and asked whether it is an extended system like Otto. Tested 20 queries in four conditions: paragraph retrieval, section retrieval, no retrieval with default prompt, no retrieval with the same persona prompt.
numbers: 20 queries; gpt-3.5-turbo-1106; 20 paragraph chunks or 5 section chunks retrieved per query; text-embedding-ada-002, L2 distance. Evaluation was qualitative, no scores.
limits: Small qualitative test, no rater scores. Mostly a philosophical argument, not a performance benchmark.
agent_relevance: Direct template for treating a vector store or notes file as Otto's notebook; shows what to test (is the note actually used).

source: Smart, Clowes and Clark (2025) - redundancy problem
finding: Persona prompt alone (no retrieval) gave answers close to the retrieval versions on some questions, e.g. wideware and 'Who is Otto?'. So the model already held much of the content in its weights. This weakens the parity with Otto, whose MoMA address is not in his head.
numbers: Condition GPTMODIFIED beat GPTDEFAULT on the 20 queries; for some queries it approximated the retrieval conditions.
quote: the base GPT model was still able to generate reasonable responses
limits: Holds for well-known content. The authors reply with an Inga-uses-notebook variant: what matters is the action-guiding role, not that internal recall was possible.
agent_relevance: Our notes must hold facts the model lacks, otherwise the note adds nothing. Test with a no-note control.

source: Smart, Clowes and Clark (2025) - agency problem
finding: In Digital Andy the app, not the model, triggers retrieval and builds the prompt. The authors say this differs from Otto, who decides to consult the notebook. It is unclear whether the model is the subject of extension or the app is.
numbers: Qualitative argument; the app embeds the query, retrieves, posts the prompt, returns the answer.
quote: it is the App that retrieves information from the vector database
limits: Authors call the matter not cut and dried. Agent loops where the model issues the memory call may fit better.
agent_relevance: Design the agent so the model itself decides when to read and write notes (MemGPT style), to meet the Otto condition of active use.

source: Smart, Clowes and Clark (2025) - use-versus-ignore test
finding: The redundancy problem is solved only if the model actually factors in retrieved text. If it ignores it and relies on parametric memory, the vector store is not part of its memory. This was proposed, not measured.
numbers: No count of how often the model used retrieved chunks. The app has a tracer listing retrieved chunks.
limits: The test was not run.
agent_relevance: Add a test: change a note, see if the answer changes. If not, the note is not coupled.

source: Clark (2025) Extending Minds with Generative AI, Nature Communications 16:4627
finding: Clark argues generative AI tools are one more case of hybrid thinking systems. Risks he names: judging that you know more than you do after online search, over-estimating unaided quiz performance, uncritical acceptance. His remedy is better judgement of when to trust a resource and when to use biological memory.
numbers: No new data. Cites studies on GPS and hippocampus, search-induced overconfidence, attention span. Page showed 113 citations and 77k accesses.
quote: we both trust and question the suggestions of the more personalized resource
limits: Position piece. Does not test LLM agents.
agent_relevance: Supports weighing trust per source (note, tool, own recall) rather than accepting all retrieved text.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT: Towards LLMs as Operating Systems
finding: Model manages its own memory tiers through function calls (main context, working context, archival and recall storage), with a memory-pressure warning at about 70% of context. It pages information in and out. This is an agent that itself decides to use its external store.
numbers: Deep memory retrieval accuracy: GPT-3.5 38.7% to 66.9% with MemGPT; GPT-4 32.1% to 92.5%; GPT-4 Turbo 35.3% to 93.4%. ROUGE-L GPT-4 0.296 to 0.814.
limits: Baselines saw only a lossy summary of past sessions; benchmark built by the authors with an LLM.
agent_relevance: Closest working analogue of Otto's notebook in an LLM loop; copy the memory-pressure prompt and self-managed write step.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT - nested key-value and document QA
finding: Fixed-context GPT-3.5 hit 0% at one nesting level of key-value lookups; GPT-4 and GPT-4 Turbo hit 0% by three levels. MemGPT with GPT-4 stayed accurate at all levels by repeating lookups. With GPT-3.5, MemGPT did poorly due to weak function calling.
numbers: Nested KV: 0% at 1 level (GPT-3.5), 0% by 3 levels (GPT-4 baselines); MemGPT with GPT-4 unaffected. Document QA: baseline capped at retriever quality; MemGPT not limited by context size.
limits: Synthetic UUID task. Needs strong function-calling models; MemGPT with GPT-4 Turbo was worse than with GPT-4.
agent_relevance: Looping over an external store beats one-shot context for multi-hop facts, but only for models that call tools reliably.

source: Packer et al. (2023) MemGPT - queue manager
finding: Eviction policy: warning at about 70% of context, flush at 100%, evict about 50%, make a recursive summary; evicted messages stay in recall storage.
numbers: Thresholds 70% warn, 100% flush, 50% evicted.
limits: Fixed thresholds chosen by the authors, not tuned in the paper.
agent_relevance: A concrete rule for when the agent must save notes before context runs out.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents: Interactive Simulacra of Human Behavior
finding: Memory stream in natural language, retrieval by recency, importance and relevance, plus reflection and planning. Ablating memory types lowered believability in human rankings; the full architecture was best and beat crowdworker-written answers.
numbers: 100 evaluators ranked 5 conditions. TrueSkill mu: full 29.89 (sd 0.72); no reflection 26.88; no reflection or planning 25.64; crowdworker 22.95; no memory, planning or reflection 21.21. Kruskal-Wallis H(4)=150.29, p<0.001.
limits: Believability ranking, not task success. 25 agents, two game days.
agent_relevance: Notes help most when retrieved by a scored rule and when synthesised into higher-level notes.

source: Park et al. (2023) Generative Agents - failure modes
finding: Most common errors: failing to retrieve a relevant memory, inventing details around a real memory, and inheriting formal speech from the model.
numbers: Reported qualitatively; no error rates in sections read.
limits: No rates.
agent_relevance: Verify retrieved notes against the source; guard against embellishment.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Agent writes verbal reflections after failures into an episodic memory buffer used in later trials. No weight updates. The written note is the learning.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%. ALFWorld: 130 of 134 tasks in 12 trials, absolute +22%. HotPotQA +20%. Self-reflection gave +8% absolute over episodic memory of the last raw trajectory (100 questions). Memory limited to last 3 reflections; ReAct-only plateaued at 22% hallucination.
limits: Needs reliable self-evaluation or an environment signal; code uses 1 reflection; HotPotQA sample 100.
agent_relevance: A written note on why a try failed beats a raw log; cap notes at a few.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion - failure analysis
finding: Common baseline error: the agent believes it holds an item that it does not; reflection removes most such cases. Reflection is triggered by simple rules.
numbers: Trigger: same action and response for more than 3 cycles, or over 30 actions.
limits: Triggers are hand-written heuristics.
agent_relevance: Simple loop-detection triggers can decide when to write a note.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with LLMs
finding: Skill library of verified code, retrieved by embedding of the description (top 5). It grows, compounds, and transfers to a new world. Without it, progress plateaus late.
numbers: 63 unique items in 160 iterations, 3.3x prior SOTA; wooden tools 15.3x, stone 8.5x, iron 6.4x faster; 2.3x longer distances; only agent reaching diamond. Removing self-verification: -73% items.
limits: Minecraft only, GPT-4 only; few runs.
agent_relevance: The library in our schema: store only verified skills, index by description, retrieve a few.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager - code as memory
finding: A skill is stored only after self-verification passes; the agent retries up to 4 rounds, then asks for another task.
numbers: Top-5 skills retrieved; 4 code rounds max.
limits: Minecraft specific.
agent_relevance: Write to the library only after a test passes.

source: Nye et al. (2021) Show Your Work: Scratchpads for Intermediate Computation
finding: Letting the model write intermediate steps to a scratchpad improves multi-step computation, including out-of-distribution addition. The scratchpad is an external working store inside the text.
numbers: Synthetic Python execution (200 test problems): direct 11% few-shot, 20% fine-tuned; scratchpad 26.5% few-shot (loosened criterion), 41.5% fine-tuned. 137B model. MBPP-aug: scratchpad model solves over 3 times more tasks than with original data.
limits: 137B model; few-shot criterion loosened; not about persistent notes.
agent_relevance: The written trace is part of the computation, a cheap constituent of cognition.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
finding: Accuracy has a U shape over where the relevant passage sits: best at start or end, worst in the middle. A middle placement can be worse than having no documents.
numbers: GPT-3.5-Turbo with the answer in the middle scored below its closed-book 56.1% on multi-document QA. Extended-context models often matched short-context ones.
limits: 2023 models; later models may differ.
agent_relevance: Order notes: most relevant at start or end of the prompt; keep the set short.

source: Liu et al. (2023) Lost in the Middle - key-value task
finding: Even base models without instruction tuning show the U shape; encoder-decoder models are robust only within training length.
numbers: Synthetic key-value task used as a minimal test; numbers not extracted.
limits: Not extracted.
agent_relevance: Position effects are architectural; reorder notes rather than hope.

source: Maharana et al. (2024) Evaluating Very Long-Term Conversational Memory of LLM Agents (LoCoMo)
finding: 50 dialogues of 300 turns (about 9K tokens avg) test memory. Long-context LLMs and RAG improve over a plain model but trail humans, most on temporal reasoning and adversarial questions.
numbers: Gains of 22-66%; still 56% below humans overall, 73% below on temporal reasoning; adversarial questions 83% lower than base model.
limits: Machine-generated dialogues with human fixing; GPT-3.5-era models.
agent_relevance: Retrieval alone does not give human-level memory; add timestamps to notes.

source: Maharana et al. (2024) LoCoMo - event graph summarization
finding: Long-context models grasp facts but misassign them to the wrong speaker.
numbers: Event graph summarization lags the base model by 14%.
limits: Abstract-level reading.
agent_relevance: Notes should record who said or did what, not only what.

source: Wu et al. (2025) LongMemEval: Benchmarking Chat Assistants on Long-Term Interactive Memory
finding: 500 questions test five memory abilities. Reading the whole 115k-token history is far worse than being given only the evidence sessions. Fact-expanded keys and time-aware query expansion help.
numbers: Long-context GPT-4o, Llama 3.1, Phi-3: 30% to 60% drop vs oracle evidence; key expansion with facts +9.4% recall@k and +5.4% accuracy; time-aware query expansion +6.8% to 11.3% recall on temporal questions.
limits: Chat-assistant setting; 50 sessions; 2024 models.
agent_relevance: Index notes by facts plus timestamps.

source: Wu et al. (2025) LongMemEval - granularity
finding: Storing by round beats storing by session. Compressing history into facts alone loses information overall but helps multi-session reasoning.
numbers: Direction of effects only; figures not extracted.
limits: Figures not extracted.
agent_relevance: Keep raw notes plus a fact index, not facts alone.

source: Xu et al. (2025) A-MEM: Agentic Memory for LLM Agents
finding: Zettelkasten-style notes that link to each other and rewrite older notes ('memory evolution'). Removing both link generation and evolution hurt most, especially multi-hop.
numbers: About 1,200 tokens per memory operation vs 16,900 for LoCoMo and MemGPT baselines, an 85-93% cut; under $0.0003 per operation. Compared on LoCoMo with LoCoMo, ReadAgent, MemoryBank, MemGPT.
limits: Authors' own runs of baselines; cost at commercial API prices.
agent_relevance: Linked, self-updating notes, like a human notebook habit, are cheap enough to keep.

source: Chhikara et al. (2025) Mem0: Production-Ready AI Agents with Scalable Long-Term Memory
finding: Extracts and consolidates salient facts from conversations. On LoCoMo it beats other memory systems; full-context is next best on accuracy but slow.
numbers: 26% relative gain in LLM-judge score over OpenAI memory; graph variant about 2% higher; 91% lower latency than full context. Open-domain J: Mem0 72.93, Mem0g 75.71, Zep 76.60 (best); multi-hop J 51.15.
limits: Vendor paper comparing its own system; LoCoMo is small.
agent_relevance: Extraction and consolidation beat raw dumps, but full context is the accuracy ceiling to beat.

source: Yao et al. (2023) ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
finding: Interleaving thought with actions on an external source (Wikipedia API) reduces hallucination and error propagation seen in chain-of-thought, and beats imitation and RL on interactive tasks.
numbers: Absolute success rate +34% on ALFWorld and +10% on WebShop over imitation and RL methods.
limits: Few-shot prompted, 2022 models; QA gains depend on API quality.
agent_relevance: The act-and-read loop is the base coupling between model and world.

source: Schick et al. (2023) Toolformer: Language Models Can Teach Themselves to Use Tools
finding: Model learns, self-supervised, which APIs to call, when, with what arguments, and how to use the result. Tools: calculator, Q&A, search, translation, calendar. The model itself decides when to offload.
numbers: Abstract and method read; no per-task numbers recorded.
limits: Numbers not extracted; needs fine-tuning, unlike a pure scaffold.
agent_relevance: Learning when to offload is itself a skill; supports a schema step that decides note use.

source: Sumers et al. (2024) Cognitive Architectures for Language Agents (CoALA)
finding: Frames language agents with working memory, episodic, semantic and procedural long-term memory, and internal versus external actions (retrieval, reasoning, grounding). Maps Reflexion, Voyager, Generative Agents onto it.
numbers: Survey; no benchmark numbers recorded.
limits: Conceptual; read for structure only.
agent_relevance: Gives words for our notes (episodic) and library (procedural).

source: Kosmyna et al. (2025) Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt
finding: Humans writing essays with an LLM had weaker brain connectivity and poorer memory of their own essays than search or brain-only users. Offloading replaced encoding instead of extending memory.
numbers: 54 participants in sessions 1-3, 18 in session 4. Session 1 quoting own essay: 83.3% (15/18) of LLM group failed vs 11.1% (2/18) of Search and Brain-only. Session 4: LLM-to-Brain 1/9 correct quote vs Brain-to-LLM 7/9. EEG connectivity scaled down with external support.
limits: Preprint under review; small samples; essay task; EEG reading contested.
agent_relevance: A note extends the mind only if integrated; add read-back checks.

source: Lee et al. (2025) Impact of Generative AI on Critical Thinking (CHI 2025)
finding: Higher confidence in the AI went with less critical thinking; higher self-confidence went with more.
numbers: 319 knowledge workers; 936 first-hand examples. Page gave no effect sizes.
limits: Self-report survey; only the abstract page was read.
agent_relevance: Calibrated trust in the tool is the lever; check retrieved notes in proportion to doubt.
